If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (days 1–7) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (days 1–7) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment swings from positive to negative mid-cycle (day 10–15), shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% in mid-horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in late horizon (days 20–30) to capture momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in late horizon (days 20–30) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33) across recent days, apply a 1–2% smoothing dampener across all horizons to reduce overfitting to short-term noise.
